issues.legal_issue: A competing business operator cannot challenge permission for the relocation of an existing mill solely because the relocation may adversely affect its business, even if the required prior permission was not obtained.
material_facts: An existing rice mill had to relocate after its land and buildings were acquired, and the state allotted it a new site.
The mill’s machinery was moved before the location-change permission was issued, but milling operations at the new site had not begun before permission was granted.
A nearby competing mill objected that the relocation would adversely affect its business and challenged the permission.
The relocated mill complied with the statutory requirements for carrying on milling operations at the new site.
issues.conclusion: The competing operator had no standing to challenge the permission because the alleged failure to obtain prior permission did not infringe a right vested in it; the relocation could not be prevented merely because it might harm a competitor’s business.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8(3)(c) of the Rice Milling Industry (Regulation) Act, 1958, a mill owner must obtain prior permission to change the location of a licensed mill; non-compliance may expose the owner to a penalty under section 13. The restriction is regulatory and does not give a competitor an independent right to prevent another person from carrying on business. Article 19(1)(g) protects the right to carry on business, subject to restrictions imposed by law in the interests of the general public under Article 19(6). No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: relocation_permission_challenge and existing_mill_relocated and objector_is_competitor and objection_is_only_adverse_business_effect and no_objector_right_is_infringed

predicates.relocation_permission_challenge: A person challenged permission for the relocation of an existing business operation.
predicates.existing_mill_relocated: The owner moved an existing mill to a different location.
predicates.objector_is_competitor: The person challenging the permission operated a competing business.
predicates.objection_is_only_adverse_business_effec: The objector relied on the prospect that the relocation would adversely affect its business.
predicates.no_objector_right_is_infringed: The permission did not infringe a right vested in the objector.

issues.definition: When a competitor challenges permission for an existing mill’s relocation based only on adverse business effects, and no right vested in the competitor is infringed, the competitor lacks standing.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory factors for permitting a new or defunct mill do not govern permission to change the location of an existing mill.
material_facts: The mill had been operating for many years and was an existing mill, rather than a new or defunct mill.
The authority permitted the mill to change its location after the original site was acquired for a public project and an alternative site was allotted.
The objector argued that the authority had to consider the factors specified for permits to establish or recommence a mill, including the number of mills in the locality and effects on employment.
The state had arranged the alternative site and relocation to reduce hardship resulting from the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The authority was not statutorily required to consider the factors specified for granting a permit to a new or defunct mill when deciding whether to permit relocation of an existing mill; the permission was not shown to have been granted without consideration of relevant circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5(1), 5(3) and 5(4) of the Rice Milling Industry (Regulation) Act, 1958 concern permits for establishing a new mill or recommencing operations in a defunct mill. Section 6 provides for licences, and section 8(3)(c) makes prior permission for a change of location a condition applicable to a licensed mill. The authority must consider the expediency of permitting the location change, but section 5(4) does not impose a duty to consider its listed factors in deciding that question. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.existing_mill_relocation_permission_proc: The proceeding concerns permission for an existing mill to relocate.
predicates.mill_is_existing: The mill was operating as an existing mill, rather than being new or defunct.
predicates.permission_is_for_location_change: The authority was asked to permit a change in the mill’s location.

issues.definition: If a proceeding concerns permission to relocate an existing mill, the factors applicable to permits for new or defunct mills are not mandatory considerations for that permission.
